newsitem.title: INDIA: Mother Teresa has chest pain but all right - doctors.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa has chest pain but all right - doctors.

text.p: Mother Teresa suffered slight chest pain early on Thursday but recovered to eat her breakfast and say prayers, doctors said.
"She had some problem around 6:45 a.m. (0115 GMT)," Calcutta's B.M. Birla Heart Research Centre said in a regular update on the 86-year-old Roman Catholic missionary's condition.
"She felt uncomfortable following slight chest pain. It is all right now. She had her morning tea and prayer."
Last month the 1979 Nobel peace prize winner underwent surgery to clear two blocked coronary arteries. She had similar surgery in 1991 in the United States and in 1993 at the Birla clinic.

On Wednesday, doctors gave her a mild electric shock to correct her irregular heart beat. Afterwards they said the procedure, during which Mother Teresa remained conscious but under sedation, was a success.
But the eight-member team of doctors said on Thursday that the revered missionary's health remained at risk.
"Mother Teresa's condition remained unchanged yesterday. She is still not out of danger," the latest medical update said.
Mother Teresa's recovery has been complicated by bronchial pneumonia.

The revered missionary has been pressing doctors to let her return to her Missionaries of Charity religious order to resume her work with the sick and dying, which won her the title "Saint of the Gutters".
But doctors have cautioned that her recovery will be slow, and she might never be as active as before.
